findings.accepted_because: The minor compression slip is real and verified against sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex:22 and Bede's bound Luke 21:28--29 and 32--33 witnesses, but repairing it would disturb settled prose on a tightly balanced 12-page concise layout while a reader who never learns that Bede transmitted Gregory on vv. 28--29 is not misled about Gregory's exposition of vv. 28--29 (already summarized at lines 11 and 19) or Bede's actual teaching on Luke 21:32--33.
findings.problem: At sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:21, compression of sections/04-lane-eschatological.tex:22 omitted the clause stating that St. Bede transmits St. Gregory's exposition of Luke 21:28--29 while retaining the opening scope phrase 'On vv.~28--29 and~32--33, St.~Bede (\work{In Lucae Evangelium Expositio}~VI) notes that \latin{Amen}...' ahead of a sentence whose entire content comes from v. 32 (followed by a separate sentence 'On verse~33...'). As a result, vv. 28--29 (also listed in sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:19 as 'on Luke~21:28--29, 32--33') receives no explicit exposition in the concise study.
findings.required_result: If sections/13-concise-commentary.tex:21 is reopened in a future edit, either add a brief clause noting that Bede transmits Gregory on vv. 28--29 before explaining Amen and generatio haec on v. 32, or narrow the lead-in to 'On verse~32' and trim '28--29,' from sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex:19.

summary: Independent cold review of the concise study for the 1962 Roman Rite First Sunday of Advent (src/gemini/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/01-first-sunday-of-advent/synthesis.tex, sections/10-concise-inventory.tex through sections/14-concise-apparatus.tex, and generated/scriptural-date-location-page.tex) passes with zero blocking findings and one accepted minor finding (SYN-006). Reading the concise study alone before consulting sections/01--09 cleanly recovered all three distinct whole-formulary interpretations (Strict Judge, Incarnational & Marian, Conversion & Altar Bridge), their governing questions, patristic reasoning, interleaved cross-proper comparisons, and four-sense distinctions; subsequent line-by-line comparison against the accepted expansive study, propers/verified.md, and direct bound witnesses in src/sources/ (including St. Augustine, De civitate Dei XX.14, 16, and 24 in NPNF I.2; St. Bede, In Lucae Evangelium Expositio VI on Luke 21:28--29, 32--33; St. Gregory the Great, Hom. in Evang. 1; St. Ambrose, Exp. in Luc. X.37--45; St. Cyril of Alexandria, Sermon CXXXIX; St. John Chrysostom, Hom. in Rom. 24; St. Augustine, Enarr. in Ps. 24 and 84, Sermo 185.1, and Confessions VIII.12.29; St. Thomas Aquinas, Postilla on Ps. 24; St. Robert Bellarmine; St. Bernard of Clairvaux; St. Leo the Great; Bl. Ildefonso Schuster; William Durandus; Sicard of Cremona; John Beleth; Rupert of Deutz; Dom Prosper Gueranger; and Cornelius a Lapide) confirmed verbatim quotation accuracy, faithful upstream synchronization of Augustine XX.14/16/24 vs. Bede on Luke 21:33 across sections/11--14, preserved textual qualifications (Old Latin suavitatem, omitted Rom. 13:14b, Schuster not invoking Bernard's Middle Coming), strict 1962 isolation, plain non-jargon prose, and passing read-only preflight, component, chronology, and metadata checks. Concrete Page-2 lookup on the generated orientation-v3 table (research/chronology-table.tex and research/chronology-annotations.tex) succeeded across all seven directly appointed scriptural propers: looking up Gospel: Luke 21:25--33 cleanly separates Narrated event ('Jesus teaches in Jerusalem about the coming of the Son of Man' -> 'Date unresolved') from Composition ('The Gospel of St Luke' -> 'Disputed: c. A.D. 70; Before Acts and the end of Paul's Roman imprisonment'), and looking up Introit: Ps. 24:1--3 (Vg.; Heb. 25), Ps. 24:4 (Vg.; Heb. 25) cleanly pairs Traditional attribution ('David's reign in the usual chronology; Hebron, then Jerusalem' -> 'c. 1055--1015 B.C. (usual chronology; Corbett also reports dates 30--50 years later)'), Historical setting ('Occasion date unresolved'), and Composition ('Psalms' -> 'Before c. 165 B.C.'), with Alleluia: Ps. 84:8 (Vg.; Heb. 85) and Epistle: Rom. 13:11--14 similarly legible without traversing columns. Meaningful limits: this is a source-level cold review and does not compile or visually inspect a print PDF, so physical pagination is not independently certified here; remote/restricted upstream holdings noted in research/scope.md remain outside the concise study's claims; and one minor compression slip on Bede's vv. 28--29 citation scope (SYN-006) is recorded as accepted without blocking.
